title.narrative: Emergency Response to Support conflict displaced populations in Fashoda and Melut counties, Upper Nile State, South Sudan

description.narrative: HepAge will provide Shelter and NFIs assistance to 1300 HHs /7800 individuals (IDP and Host communities ) 2574 Women, 2262 Men, 1404 Boys and 1560 Girls) people with in Kind ESNFI assistance for 1000 HHs and Cash for ESNFI for 300 HHs for particularly, highly vulnerable communities group like single mothers, older persons and people with disabilities: The project aims to save lives, alleviate suffering and improve the living conditions of IDPs in collective centers, IDPs in the host community and affected host community through provision of emergency shelter and essential non-food items, targeting women (especailly Pregnant women and lactating mothers), children (girls and boys), older people and persons with disabilities and their households. Specifically, the response will focus on (1) providing the crisis affected IDPs and host communities with essential NFIs packages which include mosquito nets, plastic sheets and floor mats to protect them against malaria and 2) provision of conditional cash assistance for shelters construction to the most vulnerable categories, particularly single mothers, children, older persons and Persons with Disabilities to address their safety and protection risks. This is in line with the lack of shelters, essential NFIs, overcrowding and protection risks identified in the Inter-agency Assessment reports. The proposed intervention will ensure that crisis-affected people have access to adequate, appropriate shelters, and essential household items that enables them to live in safe, secure and dignfied environment. During implemention, due consideration will be given to a range of cross-cutting issues essential to a comprehensive and inclusive response, by emphasising on DO NO HARM principles and practices, targeting the most vulnerable and inclusion of older persons and PwDs.

The proposed response will address the needs and gaps of 35,505 Individuals (31868 IDPs and 10% of Host communities 3187 individual (11,568 Women, 10,166 Men, 6310 Boys and 7011 Girls) people identified in the assessment by providing life-saving Multi-Purpose Cash assistance ,Shelter NFIs ,WASH . Health and GBV and Protection interventions.
